title: Faster and Cheaper: Measure Before You Tune
intro: 'Make it faster' and 'make it cheaper' are the same job more often than people expect: wasted CPU is wasted money, and over-provisioning is usually a guess made because nobody measured. This path starts with measurement, moves to finding where time actually goes, and ends with turning what you learned into right-sized resources and a smaller bill.
resolution: Every improvement here started with a number, not a hunch: a percentile instead of an average, a profile instead of a guess about which function is slow, a utilisation graph instead of the size someone picked two years ago. The afternoon slowdown was a burstable instance running out of CPU credits, which the application's own CPU graph could never show; the CloudWatch bill was a log level, not a launch. Rightsizing and autoscaling only save money once requests reflect real use, and the cluster's cost only gets owners once it's split by team. Measure, change one thing, measure again.
